title: Freedom kept: the power to act otherwise in the divided sense
source_text: LXIII. Neque propterea quicquam praejudicari putant libertati voluntatis humanae; quoniam gratia Dei sic movet & determinat liberum arbitrium creatum ad agendum, ut ab eo non tollat potestatem aliter agendi: ita ut posita gratia, agat quidem infallibiliter, sed semper in sensu diviso potens sit non agere, aut aliter agere.
pass_a_gloss: LXIII. Nor on that account do they think anything is prejudiced to the freedom of the human will; since the grace of God so moves and determines created free choice to act, that it does not take from it the power of acting otherwise: so that grace being posited, it acts indeed infallibly, but always in the divided sense it is able not to act, or to act otherwise.
pass_b_english: Thesis LXIII. They do not think this harms the freedom of the human will in any way. God's grace moves and determines created free choice to act in such a way that it does not remove its power to act otherwise.
So when grace is given, the will does act without fail, yet in the divided sense it always remains able not to act or to act otherwise.

lemmas.latin: ut ab eo non tollat potestatem aliter agendi
lemmas.gloss: that it does not take from it the power of acting otherwise

lemmas.latin: in sensu diviso potens sit non agere
lemmas.gloss: in the divided sense it is able not to act

choices.why: Thomist terms of art (physical premotion) for God's causally prior motion of the will; kept as technical terms.
